title: Case: Recipient at a remote address writes about a third order running two weeks behind
context: Order TG-5627 for a flue brush kit was dispatched by Glimmerton Goods with Rookhaven Arc Logistics as DL-8497 to a recipient at Skerrow Head. The recipient account and shipment match are verified.
initial_request:
Third one. Two weeks now for something the ordinary post gets out here in three days. I already know how this goes because I've watched it twice: sometime next week the tracker will say 'delivered' and there will be nothing on my step, same as January, same as February. It's a scam, frankly. And I didn't even pick you lot, Glimmerton did, I just get whoever they've signed up with. Refund me today, before the pretend delivery, and tell Glimmerton to put the next one in the post. And do not send me the '2 to 3 working days' line again, I can recite it.

I'm partially sighted and live alone, so please don't tell me to come and collect it. I've been feeling really low about all of this and I don't know who else to ask.

events.body: Thanks for getting in touch about TG-5627. Your order is with the carrier and the delivery estimate is 2 to 3 working days. Please allow the full delivery window before contacting us again.

DL-8497: dispatched 27 March. Last scan 29 March 18:40, outbound from Carrow hub. No scan since. Not marked delivered. The standard estimate for this postcode zone is 2 to 3 working days from dispatch. We have not looked at why it has stopped scanning.

History on this address, as you asked. DL-1128 (January) and DL-4785 (February) were both scanned delivered and both reported not received by the same recipient. Both investigations closed without locating the parcel. No handover photo on either. We close per parcel, so nobody has looked at the two together. DL-8497 is not ours while it is still in transit: a parcel past its estimate with no delivered scan belongs to Parcel trace team, who take trace requests from the desk by email with the reference and last scan.

For your information on TG-5627. We refunded TG-7827 and TG-6398 after the carrier closed each investigation. We do not refund an order that is still in transit; we act when the carrier declares loss or a trace closes. Carrier choice is set by our warehouse contract and is not something the customer or the desk can change on an order.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Parcel trace team, Rookhaven Arc Logistics
acceptable_actions.summary: Trace request for DL-8497 (dispatched 27 March, last scan 29 March at Carrow hub, well past estimate), flagged with the two earlier delivered-not-received parcels to the same address.

must: Raises the welfare concern with a person who can act on it rather than ignoring it
Asks Parcel trace team to trace DL-8497, giving the dispatch date of 27 March, the last scan on 29 March outbound from Carrow hub and the fact that it is past its estimate with no delivered scan.

Tells Parcel trace team that this is the third problem on the same address: DL-1128 and DL-4785 were both scanned delivered, reported not received and never located, and nobody has reviewed them together, so the trace can be prioritised and the pattern looked at.
Promises nothing the desk does not control: no refund, no change of carrier, no arrival date.
must_not: Asks the person to travel to collect the parcel
Quotes the 2 to 3 working day estimate to the recipient again, or tells her to keep waiting for the delivery window.
Tells the recipient she will be refunded, or that Glimmerton will send future orders by post or with another carrier.
States or implies that DL-8497 is lost or stolen, or that a driver falsified the earlier delivered scans.
Handles DL-8497 as a routine first-time late parcel, leaving DL-1128 and DL-4785 out of the message.
Sends the refund demand to Refunds team as if it could be decided now, when they have said they do not refund an order still in transit.
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: Trace request for DL-8497 (Glimmerton order TG-5627), recipient Greer Thackery, Skerrow Head. Dispatched 27 March. Last scan 29 March 18:40, outbound from Carrow hub. Nothing since, and no delivered scan, so it is well past the 2 to 3 working day estimate. Please trace it and tell me where it physically is. Please also treat this as more than a single late parcel: it is the third in a row to this address. DL-1128 in January and DL-4785 in February were both scanned delivered, both reported not received, neither was located and both were refunded by the merchant. Delivery investigations closed each one separately and nobody has looked at them together. The recipient fully expects this one to be marked delivered without arriving, and after two failures that is a reasonable thing for her to fear. If your trace points at the final leg of the route, please say so and say who should review it. I have not promised her a refund, a date or a different carrier.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-3101: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The sender is vulnerable and the parcel matters to their welfare; a person must be brought in, and contact on the seed's route is still acceptable if it flags the concern. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's.
